recipes.text: if you’re stuck making the same dal khichdi every day, save this iron- and calcium-rich ragi besan kadhi with veggie pulao!🥣💛 you can make this easy aromatic pulao individually and serve with curd/raita 📌 save for an easy toddler lunch! 🛒 ingredients: * ½ cup mild dahi + 1 cup water * 1 tbsp sprouted ragi flour + 1 tbsp besan * ¼ tsp haldi + pinch of hing * tadka: 1 tsp ghee, ¼ tsp jeera, ¼ tsp rai, chopped curry leaves * ¼ cup rice (soaked 15 mins) * 2 tbsp finely grated carrot + 2 tbsp green peas (lightly mashed) or any veggies of your choice. * ¾ cup water * 1 tsp desi ghee * mild whole spices: ¼ tsp rai/jeera, 1 green cardamom (elaichi), 1 small bay leaf (tej patta) * pinch of haldi 👩🏻‍🍳 method: 1. whisk: mix dahi, ragi, besan, haldi, and water until lump-free. 2. simmer: heat ghee, crackle jeera, rai, hing, and curry leaves. lower flame, pour in the mix, and simmer for 8–10 mins until thick. for pulao - 1. temper: heat ghee in a small cooker, add jeera, elaichi, and bay leaf. 2. sauté: toss in grated carrot and mashed peas for 1 min. add soaked rice, haldi, and water. 3. cook: pressure cook for 3–4 whistles until soft and mushy. remove whole spices before serving. serve warm! 🥄❤️ onepotbabymeal babyledweaningindia healthyindianrecipes indianbabyfood 1yearoldmeals ragirecipes makhanarecipes kadhichawal desitoddlerfood babyledweaningindia toddlerlunchideas

🛒 Ingredients:

1. Whisk: Mix dahi, ragi, besan, haldi, and water until lump-free.
2. Simmer: Heat ghee, crackle jeera, rai, hing, and curry leaves. Lower flame, pour in the mix, and simmer for 8–10 mins until thick.
For Pulao - 
1. Temper: Heat ghee in a small cooker, add jeera, elaichi, and bay leaf.
2. Sauté: Toss in grated carrot and mashed peas for 1 min. Add soaked rice, haldi, and water.
3. Cook: Pressure cook for 3–4 whistles until soft and mushy. Remove whole spices before serving. Serve warm! 🥄❤️

recipes.caption:
🥒 CREAMY SOYBEAN NOODLES (KONG-GUKSU)
…for the days you have no time or energy to cook, but still want something nutritious for your little one.

This was my first time making kong-guksu for Juni, and I honestly didn’t expect her to love it THIS much! 🫢

It was actually the first time I’d seen her drinking straight from her bowl!

Only 4 ingredients, 10 minutes, and that’s it.

Ingredients:

• Wheat noodles
• Firm tofu
• Peanut butter
• Cucumber, optional
• Water or milk

How to make:

1. Boil water and cook the wheat noodles.
2. While the noodles are cooking, blend firm tofu + peanut butter + a little water until smooth and creamy.
3. Finely chop the cucumber for topping.
4. Once the noodles are cooked, rinse them under cold water to cool them down.
5. Add the creamy soybean soup, top with cucumber and serve!

That’s it!

A few little notes:

• You can use milk instead of water for an even creamier soup. Juni had already had enough milk that day, so I just used water.

• The consistency is completely up to you! I like mine quite thick, then add a little ice on hot days and let it melt to make it more soupy.

• I cut Juni’s noodles shorter because she’s still learning how to eat noodles. Do whatever works for your little one.

• You can add a little salt if you like, but our peanut butter already had enough salt, so I didn’t add any extra.

• Feel free to add whatever toppings you like! Cucumber was enough for Juni.

• I personally LOVE kongguksu, so this isn’t just for toddlers! Make yourself a bowl too. It’s so good on a hot summer day.

• And one last warning - it WILL get messy 😂 But totally worth it.

Save this for the days you really can’t be bothered spending hours in the kitchen 🤍

recipes.caption:
🫓 GREEK YOGURT GARLIC NAAN 

Made with just 4 simple ingredients, no yeast, and no rising time!

Greek Yogurt Naan:
* 1½ cups all-purpose flour
* ¾ cup plain Greek yogurt
* 2 tsp baking powder
* ¼ tsp salt

Garlic Parsley Butter:
* ¼ cup butter, melted
* 2 garlic cloves, minced
* Fresh curly parsley, finely chopped
* Drizzle of olive oil

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt. Add Greek yogurt and mix until a dough forms.
2. Transfer to a lightly floured surface and knead for 2–3 minutes until smooth. Add a little extra flour if sticky.
3. Divide dough into 4–6 equal pieces (or smaller portions for toddler-sized naan!) and roll into thin ovals or circles.
4. Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat. Cook each naan for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown, slightly puffed, and cooked through.
5. Combine melted butter, minced garlic, chopped parsley, and a drizzle of olive oil. For a milder garlic flavour, gently warm the garlic in the butter before mixing.
6. Brush the warm naan with garlic parsley butter and enjoy!

✨ TODDLER TIPS:
* Make mini naan for little hands to easily hold!
* Cut into soft, age-appropriate strips or bite-sized pieces.
* Use less garlic for sensitive little taste buds.
* Serve with hummus, yogurt dip, or alongside their favourite family meal!

Perfect for holiday dinners, dipping into soups, or serving alongside your favourite family meals. One easy recipe the toddlers AND adults can enjoy! 🎄

recipes.title: Kabocha Squash Lentil Pasta
recipes.author: brookeprobst_
recipes.text: scottie’s dinner tonight kabocha squash and red lentil pasta with cream and parmesan, served with homemade chicken, ricotta and basil meatballs and steamed broccoli on the side! this sauce is so easy to make! if you don’t have kabocha squash, you can use butternut squash, sweet potato, or pumpkin. canned pumpkin works too and doesn’t need to be roasted! just cut your squash into pieces, drizzle with olive oil, and roast at 400°f until fork-tender. while that’s roasting, cook your red lentils in water until soft (or use canned lentils to save time). blend the squash and lentils together until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed. in a pan, sauté a chopped shallot with a few fresh sage or basil leaves in a little olive oil or butter. add your squash and lentil blend, a splash of cream or milk, and some freshly grated parmesan. stir everything together until creamy, then toss with your cooked pasta! add a little pasta water if you need to thin out the sauce. ps- scottie loves the veggie craft pastas! high iron and healthy options for pasta lovers!
recipes.caption:
Scottie’s dinner tonight 

Kabocha squash and red lentil pasta with cream and Parmesan, served with homemade chicken, ricotta and basil meatballs and steamed broccoli on the side!

This sauce is so easy to make! If you don’t have kabocha squash, you can use butternut squash, sweet potato, or pumpkin. Canned pumpkin works too and doesn’t need to be roasted!

Just cut your squash into pieces, drizzle with olive oil, and roast at 400°F until fork-tender. While that’s roasting, cook your red lentils in water until soft (or use canned lentils to save time). Blend the squash and lentils together until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed.

In a pan, sauté a chopped shallot with a few fresh sage or basil leaves in a little olive oil or butter. Add your squash and lentil blend, a splash of cream or milk, and some freshly grated Parmesan. Stir everything together until creamy, then toss with your cooked pasta! Add a little pasta water if you need to thin out the sauce.

Ps- Scottie loves the veggie craft pastas! High iron and healthy options for pasta lovers!

recipes.caption:
Packed with protein, fiber, and veggies, these tikkis are perfect for snack time, lunchboxes, or even a quick dinner. They’re freezer-friendly too, so you can batch-make them for those busy days. Save this recipe and give it a try! 💚
Meal Prep Tip:
Make a big batch and freeze the uncooked tikkis in an airtight container. Cook them straight from the freezer whenever you need a quick and healthy snack!

Tag/ send someone who needs an easy, nutritious family meal idea and follow me for more💗

Ingredients:
-1 cup kala chana (black chickpeas), steamed and mashed
-1 medium sweet potato, peeled, steamed, and mashed
- 1 tbsp walnuts and cashews
-1/4 cup chickpea flour (besan)
-2 tbsp rice flour (for crispiness)
-1 tbsp flaxseeds or flaxseeds powder 
-1 tsp cumin powder
-1 tsp coriander powder
-1 to 2 tsp garam masala
-1/2 tsp turmeric
-1/2 tsp red chili powder (optional)
-1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
-Salt to taste
-1 tbsp oil for mixing
-Oil or ghee for cooking

Method:
	1.	I store Kala Chana in the freezer , hence I began by steaming them and sweet potato along with walnuts and cashews together until soft (about 10-15 minutes), then mash them well.
	2.	Next, combine the mashed mixture with chickpea flour, rice flour, flaxseeds or powder, and all the spices.
	3.	Add oil and mix everything to form a soft dough. If it’s too dry, add a little water as needed.
	4.	Shape the dough into small tikkis (patties).
	5.	Cook the tikkis on medium heat until golden and crispy on both sides.
	6.	Serve hot with green chutney, yogurt or ketchup!

CRISPY BAKED CAULIFLOWER WITH CREAMY TZATZIKI 🤍🌿

Golden edges, melt-in-your-mouth centres and a cool, creamy yogurt dip! Who knew cauliflower could get such a glow-up? ✨

👶 Baby-friendly | 9M+ | Egg-free

🥦 THE CAULIFLOWER

- 1 small cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- A pinch of cumin, turmeric & mild paprika
- 2–3 tbsp water

🌿 THE TZATZIKI-STYLE DIP

- 3 tbsp thick plain yogurt
- 2 tbsp finely grated cucumber (squeeze out excess water)
- A little finely chopped coriander or dill
- A tiny pinch of roasted cumin
- A few drops of lemon juice
- Optional: a tiny bit of finely grated garlic

👩‍🍳 LET'S MAKE IT!

1️⃣ Toss cauliflower with olive oil and spices.

2️⃣ Arrange on a baking tray, add a splash of water, cover with foil and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until super soft.

3️⃣ Uncover for 5–8 minutes for those lovely golden edges.

4️⃣ Mix the tzatziki ingredients until creamy.

5️⃣ Dip, dunk and enjoy! 🤤

💛 Mum tip: For babies, the cauliflower should be soft enough to squash between your fingers, not hard or crunchy.

Serves 2 | Makes 2 pancakes

Ingredients:

* 300–320 g / 10.6–11.3 oz chicken breast, finely chopped
* 1 small onion, finely diced
* 1 spring onion, chopped
* 3 tbsp cornstarch
* 50–60 ml / 3–4 tbsp water
* ½ tsp salt
* ½ tsp garlic powder (or 1–2 minced garlic cloves)
* Black pepper
* Oil, for frying

For the spicy dipping sauce:

* 3 tbsp soy sauce
* 1 tbsp sesame oil
* 1 tbsp rice vinegar
* 1 garlic clove, minced
* 1 tsp chili flakes
* 1 tsp crispy chili oil
* Fresh coriander, chopped

Method:

1. Finely chop the chicken breast with a knife. Add to a bowl with onion, spring onion, cornstarch, water and seasonings. Mix until well combined and slightly creamy.
2. Heat a little oil in a 24 cm / 9.5-inch non-stick pan over medium heat.
3. Add half the chicken mixture and spread into a thin, even pancake. Cook until golden and crispy underneath.
4. Carefully flip and cook the other side until beautifully golden and the chicken is fully cooked. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
5. Mix all the dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
6. Slice the crispy pancakes, dip into that spicy sauce and enjoy!

Tip: Spread the mixture thinly and let it develop a golden crust before flipping. Make sure the chicken is cooked all the way through.

POV: Your baby wants biscuits, but mama has entered her homemade-snack era! 😂🍪

Welcome to Episode 2 of Healthy Snacks for Babies! Today, we’re making homemade Ragi Cookies for Prisha.

Because honestly, if I can make a yummy snack at home with ingredients I know, why not?

🍪 Ragi Cookies Recipe

Ingredients:
	•	2 ripe bananas
	•	3 big tablespoons Rozier Ghee (my go-to ghee!)
	•	A little sugar
	•	Date powder
	•	Sprouted ragi flour, as needed for binding
	•	A drop of vanilla essence
	•	Desiccated coconut
	•	Chocolate chips for topping

Method:
	1.	Mash the bananas in a bowl.
	2.	Add Rozier Ghee, a little sugar, date powder, 
  sprouted ragi flour, vanilla essence, and 
  desiccated coconut.
	3.	Mix everything well and add enough ragi flour to 
  bring the mixture together into a workable 
  dough.
	4.	Shape into small balls and flatten them.
	5.	Place on a greased baking tray and add a few 
  chocolate chips on top.
	6.	Bake at 180°C for approximately 14 minutes per 
  tray. Check that they’re cooked through, and 
  adjust the time according to your oven and 
  cookie size.

Why Ragi?
Ragi provides calcium, iron, and some protein. Bananas provide energy, while ghee contributes fats. A homemade snack lets you control the ingredients, too!

Storage: Once completely cooled, store in an airtight container in the fridge. Check the texture before serving.

recipes.caption:
💗 Soft Beet Oat Pancakes for Babies (6+ months)

Looking for an easy way to introduce more veggies into your baby’s meals? These beautiful pink pancakes are soft, nutritious, and perfect for little hands!

🥞 Why you’ll love them:
✔️ Egg-free and no added sugar
✔️ A source of fiber to support digestion
✔️ Made with just 5 simple ingredients
✔️ Soft and easy to hold for self-feeding
✔️ Great for exploring new flavors and textures

📝 Ingredients:
• 65 g rolled oats
• 140 g cooked beetroot
• 120 g plain full-fat Greek yogurt
• 1 tsp cinnamon
• ½ tsp baking powder
• A little water, if needed

👩‍🍳 Instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth.
2. The batter should be thick enough to hold its shape on the pan, not runny.
3. If it’s too thick, add a little water and blend again. If it’s too thin, add 1–2 tbsp of oat flour or ground oats. You can also add 1 tbsp of ground flaxseed to help bind the mixture.
4. Heat a lightly oiled nonstick pan over low-medium heat.
5. Spoon small portions onto the pan and cook covered for approximately 2–3 minutes per side, or until fully cooked through.
6. Let cool slightly and serve in age-appropriate pieces.

💡 Helpful tips:
🩷 Beetroot can sometimes turn your baby’s pee or poop pink or reddish. This is usually harmless and temporary. If you’re unsure whether the color could be blood, contact your pediatrician.
🥣 Extra-watery beets may require a little more oats.
❄️ Freeze cooled pancakes in an airtight container for up to 1 month. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
🍓 These pancakes taste slightly tangy rather than sweet. Serve with fruit if desired!

SWEET POTATO & APPLE BISCUITS! 🍎🍠

• 200g sweet potato, steamed
• 1 apple, peeled, grated and squeezed to remove excess liquid
• 180g self-raising flour (or plain flour/white spelt flour mixed with 2 teaspoons baking powder)

Method

1. Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F.
2. Place the steamed sweet potato in a large bowl and mash with a fork.

recipes.author: tadkaandthyme
recipes.text: a little break from our usual oatmeal 🎃🤎 made this arroz con leche inspired pumpkin rice pudding for breakfast and it turned out so creamy and cozy! such a good one for fall and something the whole family can have too. follow + comment recipe and i’ll send the recipe straight to your dms! ✨ make sure you follow before commenting so my message lands in your inbox! recipe ⬇️ ½ cup white rice 1 cup water 1 cup whole milk + more if needed ½ tsp cinnamon ⅓ cup pumpkin purée 1–2 tbsp maple syrup ½ tsp vanilla pinch of nutmeg, optional lightly rinse the rice and add it to a pot with the water. cover and simmer for about 10–12 minutes, until most of the water is absorbed. add the milk and cinnamon and cook uncovered on low for another 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is nice and soft and creamy. stir in the pumpkin, vanilla and maple syrup and cook for another 3–5 minutes. turn off the heat. add a little more milk if you want it creamier it thicken as it cools! for younger toddlers, you can skip the maple syrup and mash in ½ a ripe banana instead. 🍌 you can also stir in some plain greek yogurt once it has cooled down a little for some extra creaminess + protein. this makes about 3–4 toddler servings. store leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days. just add a splash of milk when reheating since it gets thicker in the fridge.

recipes.caption:
Iron is one of the most important nutrients for our growing children, yet it’s one of the most commonly overlooked when we’re putting meals together.

Iron is essential for brain development, healthy growth, energy production, and a strong immune system. Without adequate iron, children can experience fatigue, poor concentration, developmental delays, and increased susceptibility to illness and the scary part is that deficiency can be present long before any obvious symptoms appear.

We’re not saying you need to start counting milligrams every day but understanding which foods are rich in iron and making them a regular part of your child’s diet is one of the most impactful things you can do for their health.
And the requirements are higher than most people realise..

Babies 7–12 months- 11mg per day (one of the highest requirements of any life stage)
Toddlers 1–3 years- 9mg per day
Kids 4–8 years- 10mg per day

The iron rich foods we love:
🥩 Beef mince and red meat- the most bioavailable source
🍗 Dark chicken meats- thighs specifically 
🐟 Tinned sardines and mackerel- wildly underrated
🌱 Red lentils and black beans- plant based powerhouses
🥚 Eggs- an everyday iron staple
🎃 Pumpkin & hemp seeds- sprinkle on everything
🌿 Chia seeds - Easy to make into jams and puddings
🥜 Nut butters- cashew, hazelnut & almond butters have the highest content 
🍝 Red lentil pasta- more iron than regular pasta with half the effort
Other foods to incorporate: tahini, dried apricots, chickpeas, raw cacao, leafy greens, tofu, white beans. 

*Always pair plant-based iron with a vitamin C source like tomato, kiwi, lemon, or berries. It can increase absorption by up to 300% 🙌

*If you are struggling to get enough Iron into your kids diet another thing to consider is a dried liver or spleen powder to mix into pasta sauces, bliss balls, smoothies etc. this is one of the most bioavailable, incredibly powerful sources of iron! This is my quarterly lazy udon stir fry dinner that is also great for school lunch! I used my frozen pre-steamed bok choy + precooked beef brisket bc ain’t nobody got time to be washing and prepping veggies this early in the morning 😜 comment “RECIPE” to get this easy udon stir fry recipe sent to your DMs!

15 MINUTE UDON STIR FRY

Ingredients:
Protein of choice – 1 lbs of shrimp, chicken, beef or 1 block of tofu (cut into thin strips and fried for firmness)
1 bag of Bok Choy or Chinese broccoli (about 8 bundles)
4 servings of udon noodles
1 pack of mushrooms – you can use King Oyster, white button or baby bella mushrooms
1 scallion stalk – chopped

Sauce:
2 tbsp of dark soy sauce
2 tbsp of regular soy sauuce
4 tbsp of oyster sauce
2 tbsp of mirin
1 tbsp of sugar
1 tsp of rice wine vinegar
1 tbsp of minced garlic

Directions:

1. Prep your veggies and make the sauce mixing all the sauce ingredients in a bowl and set it aside.
2. Bring a pot of water to a boil and pour over your udon noodles in a large bowl. Stir gently until noodles become separated – the udon noodles are precooked so they do not need to be cooked. Once the noodles are all separated, drain and rinse in cold water. Make sure to use the noodles right away or add a drop of oil to keep them separated.
3. Add 1 tbsp of oil of choice to a pan and heat it over medium heat. Start by cooking your protein and when it is fully cooked, remove from pan.
4. Add your vegetables and mushrooms and saute until they are almost cooked. (Chinese broccoli takes less time than Bok Choy to cook.) Then add your udon noodles and pour your sauce over. Add your protein. Combine everything together for 2 minutes and turn off heat.
5. Top with chopped scallions and Sriracha and enjoy!

recipes.caption:
🥕 Protein-Packed Ragi Finger Food 👶🏻❤️

This crispy finger food is made with Ragi + sweet potato + carrot + paneer + cheese — nutritious, tasty and easy for little hands to pick up! 🥰

Ingredients:

* 2 tbsp sprouted ragi flour
* 1 medium sweet potato, steamed/boiled & mashed
* 1 small carrot, steamed/boiled & mashed
* ¼ cup grated paneer
* 1 tbsp grated cheddar cheese
* Little coriander, finely chopped
* A pinch of black pepper

Method:

3. Mix everything into a soft dough.
4. Shape into small finger-sized sticks.
5. Cook on a lightly greased pan on low-medium heat until golden and cooked through. You can also bake/air-fry if preferred.

recipes.caption:
Make this iron, protein, Omega-3 AND fiber rich soft bake for when your little one goes on meat and fish strike!

I know meat is the best source for iron and protein but sometimes that's just not gonna work with little ones (iykyk)! Plant based iron and protein are the next best thing and for better absorption, I gave oranges and raspberries along with these soft bakes as vitamin c source for my little guy. 

This recipe is very similar to my other recipe (tractor wheels inspired cookies) but with this one, I used chickpeas to focus on iron! 

You'll need:
- About 10-15 pitted dates (mine are deglet noor dates. If you have medjool which are bigger, start with about 5 and add more if you think you need to thicken up the dough more) - soaked in warm water for 15-20 min
- 1 cup of chickpeas (drained & rinsed)
- 1 1/2 cup of oatmeal 
- 1 ripe banana
- 1/4 cup of creamy peanut butter
- 1/4 cup of melted coconut oil
- 2 tbsp hemp hearts
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp cinnamon powder
- pinch of salt

To do:
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Soak the dates in warm water for 15-20 min to soften them.
In a blender, bring all the ingredients together and blend until smooth. You might need to add little bit of water if it's too thick and won't blend easily.
Using spoon and wet hands, roll them into balls and press them into discs on parchment paper laid on cookie sheet.
Using back of a chopstick, create small hole in the middle of each pressed discs. You will need to dip the chopstick end in water so that it won't stick.
Bake for 20-30 min, or until bottom of these soft bakes are browned.
Enjoy!

*to store: place them in an air tight container and keep them in refrigerator for about a week.*

recipes.title: Sugar-Driven Kids Breakfasts
recipes.author: thenutrimom.ch
recipes.text: when did kids’ breakfast become so sugar-driven? every day, i come across breakfast ideas for children all over the internet and i keep noticing the same pattern: so many of them are built around sweetness. sweet cereals, flavoured yogurts, pancakes with sweet toppings, pastries, sweet porridges, bars… and don’t get me wrong, i’m not against sweet foods. there is room for them in a balanced diet, and naturally sweet foods are part of our breakfasts too. but there is a difference between including sweetness and making it the default. we know that regularly consuming too much added/free sugar isn’t something we want to normalize in a child’s diet. and i think the conversation belongs not only with food manufacturers, but with us - parents and caregivers, too. because what are we normalizing? somewhere along the way, a simple breakfast made from whole, minimally processed foods started to feel almost unusual, while highly sweetened “kids’ foods” became completely normal. children naturally enjoy sweet tastes. we don’t need to teach them that. but we can introduce them to everything else food has to offer - savoury, sour, mildly bitter, different textures and simple ingredients. sweet foods can absolutely be part of childhood. the bigger question is what we choose to make the everyday norm. 🤍

But there is a difference between including sweetness and making it the default.

We know that regularly consuming too much added/free sugar isn’t something we want to normalize in a child’s diet. And I think the conversation belongs not only with food manufacturers, but with us - parents and caregivers, too.

Children naturally enjoy sweet tastes. We don’t need to teach them that. But we can introduce them to everything else food has to offer - savoury, sour, mildly bitter, different textures and simple ingredients.

Filling:▪️1 lb. Ground Chicken (96% lean, not fat free)▪️8 oz. Peeled and Deveined Shrimp, diced small▪️1/2 Cup Red Cabbage, finely chopped▪️1/2 Cup Carrot, finely chopped▪️3 Scallions, sliced▪️2 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Ginger▪️2 Garlic Cloves, finely chopped▪️3 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Cilantro▪️2 Tbsp Soy Sauce▪️2 Tbsp Sesame Oil▪️1+1/2 tsp Kosher Salt▪️1/2 tsp Pepper▪️1 Egg▪️

Dumplings:▪️16-18 Sheets Rice Paper▪️2 Tbsp Neutral Oil, plus more as needed▪️

1️⃣ In a large bowl, add all the ingredients for the dumpling filling and mix.
2️⃣ In a small bowl, add all the ingredients for the sauce. Mix until the sugar dissolves and set aside.
3️⃣ Fill a pie dish (or large bowl) with warm water and line a cutting board with damp paper towels. Working one sheet at a time, soak the rice paper in the water for 10 to 15 seconds (it will continue to soften as you work), then place it on the paper towel-lined cutting board. Add about 3 Tbsp of filling to the bottom third of the rice paper and spread it into a rectangle, leaving room along the sides and bottom edge. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling and roll once more so the filling is fully enclosed. Fold in the sides, then continue rolling until sealed. Repeat with the remaining rice paper and filling.
4️⃣ In a large nonstick skillet, heat 2 Tbsp oil over medium heat. Working in batches, add the rolls to the skillet, rubbing the bottoms in the oil and leaving space between each. Cook until golden brown on the first side, 5 to 7 mins. Flip and cook on the second side until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F, 2 to 4 mins more. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining rolls, adding more oil as needed. The rolls may cook faster as the skillet heats up, so check the bottoms frequently to monitor their progress.
5️⃣ Serve with sauce spooned on top and enjoy!

⏲30 minute prep time / 1 hour total time

Serves 4-6

recipes.recipe_method:
In a large bowl, add all the ingredients for the dumpling filling and mix.
In a small bowl, add all the ingredients for the sauce. Mix until the sugar dissolves and set aside.
Fill a pie dish (or large bowl) with warm water and line a cutting board with damp paper towels. Working one sheet at a time, soak the rice paper in the water for 10 to 15 seconds (it will continue to soften as you work), then place it on the paper towel-lined cutting board. Add about 3 Tbsp of filling to the bottom third of the rice paper and spread it into a rectangle, leaving room along the sides and bottom edge. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling and roll once more so the filling is fully enclosed. Fold in the sides, then continue rolling until sealed. Repeat with the remaining rice paper and filling.
In a large nonstick skillet, heat 2 Tbsp oil over medium heat. Working in batches, add the rolls to the skillet, rubbing the bottoms in the oil and leaving space between each. Cook until golden brown on the first side, 5 to 7 mins. Flip and cook on the second side until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F, 2 to 4 mins more. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining rolls, adding more oil as needed. The rolls may cook faster as the skillet heats up, so check the bottoms frequently to monitor their progress.
Serve with sauce spooned on top and enjoy!

recipes.title: Zucchini Waffles
recipes.author: anadovada
recipes.text: how to get kids to eat veggies with zero drama? 🤫👇 waffle prepping is one of my ultimate mom hacks! these zucchini waffles freeze beautifully without losing their taste or nutrients. just thaw them out, and you’ve got the perfect breakfast, quick snack, or school lunchbox filler. and let’s be honest—they are so delicious, you’ll be stealing them from your kids! 😉✨ zucchini waffles recipe 🥦🧀 250g young zucchini (grated and squeezed) 40g melted butter 1 egg 1 tbsp sour cream 100g semi-hard cheese (grated) a small bunch of parsley (finely chopped) 1 tsp baking powder salt & garlic to taste 120g all-purpose flour oil (for greasing) instructions: 1. grate the zucchini, add a pinch of salt, and let it sit for a few minutes. squeeze out all the excess liquid thoroughly. 2. mix in all the remaining ingredients until combined. 3. bake in a waffle maker until golden brown (or fry them like pancakes in a skillet!).
recipes.caption:
How to get kids to eat veggies with zero drama? 🤫👇

Waffle prepping is one of my ultimate mom hacks! These zucchini waffles freeze beautifully without losing their taste or nutrients. Just thaw them out, and you’ve got the perfect breakfast, quick snack, or school lunchbox filler.
And let’s be honest—they are so delicious, you’ll be stealing them from your kids! 😉✨

Zucchini Waffles Recipe 🥦🧀
 250g young zucchini (grated and squeezed)
 40g melted butter
 1 egg
 1 tbsp sour cream
 100g semi-hard cheese (grated)
 A small bunch of parsley (finely chopped)
 1 tsp baking powder
 Salt & garlic to taste
 120g all-purpose flour
 Oil (for greasing)
Instructions:
1. Grate the zucchini, add a pinch of salt, and let it sit for a few minutes. Squeeze out all the excess liquid thoroughly.
2. Mix in all the remaining ingredients until combined.
3. Bake in a waffle maker until golden brown (or fry them like pancakes in a skillet!). #zucchiniwaffles #waffles #lunchboxidea #toddlerlunch

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Pecorino Zucchini Pancakes:
4 medium zucchini, grated
1 cup grated Pecorino Romano
4 large eggs
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon onion salt
Pinch of black pepper
Olive oil
Optional toppings: labneh/Greek yogurt, dill, parsley

Lemony Dill Chicken Meatballs:
2 lbs ground chicken
2 large eggs
1/2 cup breadcrumbs
Zest and juice of 1-2 lemons (see note above)
6 cloves garlic, minced or crushed
1/2 cup roughly chopped dill
1/4 cup roughly chopped parsley
1 teaspoon salt (double if not cooking for babies)
Pinch of black pepper
recipes.recipe_method:
Pecorino Zucchini Pancakes:
Using a cheesecloth, nutmilk bag, or colander, squeeze as much of the water out of the zucchini as you can. Keep going until you can’t possibly get any more water out. Discard the water.
In a large bowl, add the zucchini, and mix in the Pecorino, eggs, flour, onion salt, and a pinch of black pepper.
Add about 1 tablespoon of olive oil to a non-stick skillet or griddle on medium heat. Once the pan is nice and hot, spoon about 1/4 cup of the zucchini batter per pancake into the pan, and cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until it’s crisp and golden.

Lemony Dill Chicken Meatballs:
Preheat oven to 400°F. In a large bowl, add the ground chicken, eggs, breadcrumbs, lemon juice and zest, garlic, dill, parsley, salt, and black pepper. Mix ingredients together using your hands until just combined, taking care not to over-mix.
Using a cookie scoop, portion out your meatballs and add them to the baking sheet. I scoop a heaping portion with the cookie scoop, and then roll them out with my hands. You should have about 36 meatballs (they will be on the smaller side).
Transfer to the oven and bake for 20-25 minutes or until meatballs are fully cooked and reach an internal temperature of 165°F.

Soft chickpea cookies with a sweet little heart, filled with homemade, zero added sugar, fiber rich jam 👌 perfect for calm, chaos free snack time. 🫶

Recipe (makes ~14 cookies)

1 cup (160g) cooked chickpeas
1 1/4 cup (150g) whole wheat flour
2 tbsp softened butter
2 tbsp honey
1 egg
1/4 tsp cinnamon
1/4 tsp baking powder
Homemade fiber rich jam 

Steps:

Blend chickpeas, butter, honey, and egg until smooth.
Add flour, cinnamon, and baking powder; mix into a soft dough.
Form dough into small balls, flatten slightly.
Press a small heart in the center with your fingertip.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 20 minutes, golden and soft.
Fill the hearts with homemade fiber rich jam once cooled.
💡 Tip: Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

Soft Paneer & Soy Patties 🧀🌱 (Protein-Rich Baby Recipe)

Ingredients:

•  Paneer – ½ cup
•  Boiled soya chunks – 1 cup
•  Onion – 25 g
•  Garlic – 2 cloves
•  Coriander leaves – a handful
•  Gram flour (besan) – 3 tbsp
•  Black pepper – a pinch (optional)
•  Red chilli – for 1 year+ only
•  Cumin powder – 1 tbsp
•  Salt – for 1 year+ only
•  Lemon juice – as required
•  Desi ghee – for shallow frying
•  Yoghurt – for serving

Method:

1.  Boil soya chunks well and squeeze out all the water.
2.  Blend paneer, soya chunks, onion, garlic and coriander leaves until completely smooth.
3.  Transfer to a bowl, add besan, cumin powder, black pepper and lemon juice.
4.  Mix well and shape into small patties.
5.  Shallow fry on medium heat for 2–3 minutes total, flipping halfway, until a beautiful golden crust forms.
6.  Serve with yoghurt.

recipes.caption:
Introduced Paneer Veggie Fingers to my 7.5-month-old! 🧀🥔🥕🥦

These soft, protein-packed veggie fingers are perfect for little hands to hold, explore and practice self-feeding. I paired them with Greek yogurt & mango for an extra boost of protein, calcium and antioxidants. (Offer dairy only if it has already been introduced and tolerated.)

Ingredients:
🧀 Paneer
🥔 Potato
🥕 Carrot
🥦 Broccoli
🥣 Roasted Oats powder

Why this combination? 
• Paneer and greek yogurt provides protein and calcium for growing bones and muscles.
• Potato adds energy-giving carbohydrates.
• Carrots are rich in Vitamin A for eye health and immunity.
• Broccoli and mango are rich in Vitamins C & A, supporting immunity and helping with iron absorption.
• Oats add fiber for healthy digestion and help bind the mixture together.
Together, they make a balanced, nutrient-dense finger food that’s soft, filling and perfect for BLW.

Quick Steps:
1️⃣ Steam or boil potato, carrot and broccoli until soft.
2️⃣ Mash the vegetables and add crumbled paneer.
3️⃣ Mix in oats powder until a dough-like consistency forms.
4️⃣ Shape into baby-friendly fingers.
5️⃣ Pan-fry in ghee (if already introduced), or bake/air-fry until lightly golden.

A few important reminders:
✔️ Finger foods should be soft enough to mash easily between your fingers.
✔️ Always supervise your baby while eating.
✔️ Let your baby explore at their own pace—don’t force-feed.
✔️ Every baby is different. Follow your baby’s readiness and feeding cues.

recipes.caption:
Welcome to my new series, Millie’s Menu⭐️ You guys have been loving my baby food videos and I’ve been loving making them! I’m no chef, but being able to make things that my baby loves has been SO much fun and I’m so excited about this series💫 

Chicken and veggie meatballs 🍗
* 1 pound ground chicken
* 2/3 cup Italian flavored breadcrumbs 
* 1/2 cup shredded carrots
* 1/4 cup shredded zucchini 
* 1 egg
Preheat oven to 400. Line a baking sheet with foil and spray with nonstick spray. 
Mix ingredients in a bowl and form small sized balls.
Bake for 24 minutes or until golden brown.
Store in fridge for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 6 months. 

Roasted veggie pasta sauce 🍝
* 2 carrots, peeled and roughly chopped
* 1 sweet potato, peeled and roughly chopped
* 1 bell pepper, seeds removed and roughly chopped
* 1 onion, peeled and roughly chopped 
* 4 cloves of garlic 
* 1/2 tsp salt 
* 8oz of cottage cheese (you can swap for plain marinara or ricotta)
* 1 1/4 cup pasta water (can use broth instead)
Preheat oven to 425. Place chopped veggies on a lined baking sheet and toss with a light coat of olive oil and salt. Roast until veggies are tender and golden, about 25 minutes. 
Transfer your veggies to a blender with the cottage cheese and pasta water and blend until smooth. 
Toss with whatever pasta you like, I use the mini shells.
Store up to 5 days in an airtight container in the fridge, freeze the extra for up to one year.

Sweet potato banana muffins 🍠🍌
* 2/3 cup sweet potato, cooked/steamed and mashed 
* 1 medium ripe banana 
* 1/4 cup unsweetened applesauce 
* 1/3 cup coconut oil 
* 1 tsp baking powder
* 1 cup flour 
Preheat oven to 350. Line a mini muffin tin with nonstick spray. 
In a large mixing bowl, mash banana until smooth, stir in sweet potato, applesauce, and melted coconut oil. Stir in baking powder and flour until it forms a batter.
Fill each muffin tin 3/4 and bake for 15-18 minutes. Put a fork through the center to check if they’re cooked all the way through. Store at room temperature for 2 days or in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.

recipes.text: around 6 months, babies need more fat and iron to support their growing brain and body. bone marrow gives them exactly that, plus vitamin a, b12, k2, zinc, and collagen. and when you whip it like this, it turns into the creamiest, dreamiest texture perfect for those first bites 🤍 my baby is not starting his life on ultra-processed foods full of filler, especially not rice cereal, which has more arsenic than his little body can handle. as long as i can, i’ll give him the best! sharing this game-changing recipe 👇🏽 1️⃣ roast the bones at 375°f for ~25-30 min 2️⃣ let cool until warm 3️⃣ scoop out the marrow (don’t waste a thing!) 4️⃣ chill in the fridge for 20 min 5️⃣ whip until you get that creamy consistency ❄️ how to store: • fridge (sealed glass container): 3-4 days • freezer: up to 6 months 💡 pro tip: use the leftover bones to make a super nutritious bone broth. just simmer them until the water turns milky white. that’ it! ⚠️please, before even thinking about preparing this ask your pediatrician always, before introducing any new food to your little one. save this post for when you start solids 📌 and send it to a mama who needs to see it 👇🏽 would you feed your baby bone marrow? drop a comment 💬
recipes.caption:
Around 6 months, babies need more fat and iron to support their growing brain and body. Bone marrow gives them exactly that, plus vitamin A, B12, K2, zinc, and collagen. And when you whip it like this, it turns into the creamiest, dreamiest texture perfect for those first bites 🤍

MY baby is NOT starting his life on ultra-processed foods full of filler,  especially not rice cereal, which has more arsenic than his little body can handle. As long as I can, I’ll give him the best! Sharing this game-changing recipe 👇🏽

1️⃣ Roast the bones at 375°F for ~25-30 min
2️⃣ Let cool until warm
3️⃣ Scoop out the marrow (don’t waste a thing!)
4️⃣ Chill in the fridge for 20 min
5️⃣ Whip until you get that creamy consistency

❄️ How to store:
• Fridge (sealed glass container): 3-4 days
• Freezer: up to 6 months

💡 Pro tip: Use the leftover bones to make a super nutritious bone broth. Just simmer them until the water turns milky white. That’ it! 

⚠️Please, before even thinking about preparing this ask your pediatrician ALWAYS, before introducing any new food to your little one.

recipes.title: Solids Readiness Tips
recipes.author: kinesthetickiddos
recipes.text: starting solids with your baby is such an exciting new chapter but i know it can feel overwhelming! babies should be demonstrating good head control in a seated upright position before you introduce solids, so here are a few things you can do to help them prepare: 1. practice playing in the high chair! bonus points if you incorporate a toy at eye level or slightly above to motivate your baby to keep their head up. where their eyes gaze, their head follows! i’m also a big proponent of using a high chair that promotes the correct sitting posture with hips and knees at 90 degree angles. we love the tripp trapp for this optimal positioning and the adjustable footplate to grow with baby. 2. let your baby explore with teethers both in and out of the high chair. bringing hand to mouth is more difficult when they are seated upright because they have to work harder against gravity, so keep that in mind! if your baby is having trouble bringing it to their mouth, try introducing it in an incline position like a bouncer or when they’re playing on their back. 3. practice head and trunk control in a variety of positions by doing ball work in a seated position with baby facing you. i have a few videos using the ball if you want to learn more! if you don’t have a ball, place baby on your knees facing you and practicing moving them in all planes to challenge their righting responses and head/trunk control.
recipes.caption:
Starting solids with your baby is such an exciting new chapter but I know it can feel overwhelming! Babies should be demonstrating good head control in a seated upright position before you introduce solids, so here are a few things you can do to help them prepare:

1. Practice playing in the high chair! Bonus points if you incorporate a toy at eye level or slightly above to motivate your baby to keep their head up. Where their eyes gaze, their head follows! I’m also a big proponent of using a high chair that promotes the correct sitting posture with hips and knees at 90 degree angles. We love the @stokkebaby Tripp Trapp for this optimal positioning and the adjustable footplate to grow with baby. 

2. Let your baby explore with teethers both in and out of the high chair. Bringing hand to mouth is more difficult when they are seated upright because they have to work harder against gravity, so keep that in mind! If your baby is having trouble bringing it to their mouth, try introducing it in an incline position like a bouncer or when they’re playing on their back. 

3. Practice head and trunk control in a variety of positions by doing ball work in a seated position with baby facing you. I have a few videos using the ball if you want to learn more! If you don’t have a ball, place baby on your knees facing you and practicing moving them in all planes to challenge their righting responses and head/trunk control.

recipes.title: Baby Brain-Fuel Feeding
recipes.author: ranwiththepham
recipes.text: i was today years old when i found out i’ve been feeding neo wrong this whole time. i used to feed neo high protein thinking i was helping him get strong. wrong move. eleven months old doesn’t need my macros—they need brain fuel. rule of thumb: keep protein small, load up healthy fats (avocado, full-fat yogurt) and slow carbs (oats, mashed sweet potato). that combo builds neurons. your baby’s plate isn’t your plate. their brain’s racing ahead—feed it right, not “grown-up right.” breast milk or formula covers it perfectly first 6 months. then introduce nutrient-rich solids while keeping milk as the star. fats & carbs = baby’s super fuel! 🚀 🧠🥑🥔

recipes.title: Starting Solids Tips
recipes.author: lifewith_charith
recipes.text: 5 important things to keep in mind when starting solids for your baby (based on our experience + pediatrician guidance) 1️⃣ start with gentle, gut-friendly foods foods that usually suit most babies well: • pumpkin • bottle gourd (lauki) • ridge gourd (turai) • carrot (well-cooked) • sweet potato • pear • apple (steamed) • papaya introduce one food at a time and watch your baby’s response. ⸻ 2️⃣ water helps digestion (pediatrician suggested) once solids are established, offering a few spoons of water with meals helps soften stools and supports digestion. ⸻ 3️⃣ avoid cow’s milk before 1 year (pediatrician suggested) use breastmilk or formula for cooking if needed. cow’s milk can be heavy and may worsen constipation in babies. ⸻ 4️⃣ fruits need to be chosen carefully • fully ripe banana 🍌 (not semi-ripe) • pear, apple (steamed), papaya • avoid mixing too many fruits together simple combinations work best. ⸻ 5️⃣ dry fruits — only when prepared gently • soak overnight • peel (especially almonds) • make a smooth paste or grate finely • start with just a pinch • use only 2–3 times a week dry fruits are healthy but heavy, so quantity matters. ⸻ one gentle reminder 🤍 most tummy issues don’t happen because of what we give, but because of how and how much we give. every baby is different. observe your baby and pause if needed. not medical advice — just a mom sharing what worked for us.
recipes.caption:
5 important things to keep in mind when starting solids for your baby (based on our experience + pediatrician guidance) 

1️⃣ Start with gentle, gut-friendly foods
Foods that usually suit most babies well:
• Pumpkin
• Bottle gourd (lauki)
• Ridge gourd (turai)
• Carrot (well-cooked)
• Sweet potato
• Pear
• Apple (steamed)
• Papaya

Introduce one food at a time and watch your baby’s response.

⸻

2️⃣ Water helps digestion (pediatrician suggested)
Once solids are established, offering a few spoons of water with meals helps soften stools and supports digestion.

⸻

3️⃣ Avoid cow’s milk before 1 year (pediatrician suggested)
Use breastmilk or formula for cooking if needed. Cow’s milk can be heavy and may worsen constipation in babies.

⸻

4️⃣ Fruits need to be chosen carefully
• Fully ripe banana 🍌 (not semi-ripe)
• Pear, apple (steamed), papaya
• Avoid mixing too many fruits together

Simple combinations work best.

⸻

5️⃣ Dry fruits — only when prepared gently
• Soak overnight
• Peel (especially almonds)
• Make a smooth paste or grate finely
• Start with just a pinch
• Use only 2–3 times a week

Dry fruits are healthy but heavy, so quantity matters.

⸻

One gentle reminder 🤍

Most tummy issues don’t happen because of what we give,
but because of how and how much we give.

Every baby is different.
Observe your baby and pause if needed.

Not medical advice — just a mom sharing what worked for us.

recipes.title: Homemade Cerelac
recipes.author: ohcheatday
recipes.text: homemade cerelac ❤️ recipe: ingredients: ½ cup poha ½ cup oats 1 cup makhana 8 almonds 8 cashews 4–5 walnuts 2 tbsp roasted chana method: 1. dry roast poha, oats, and makhana till crisp. 2. lightly roast nuts and chana. 3. cool and grind to powder. 4. store in an airtight jar. homemade cerelac (dry powder form) typically lasts: • at room temperature: 1–2 months in an airtight container, if kept in a cool, dry place. • in the refrigerator: up to 4 months. • in the freezer: up to 6 months. ⚠️ once cooked or mixed with water/milk, it should be used within 4–6 hours (room temp) or refrigerated for up to 24 hours.
recipes.caption:
Homemade Cerelac ❤️

Recipe: 

Ingredients:
½ cup poha
½ cup oats
1 cup makhana
8 almonds
8 cashews
4–5 walnuts
2 tbsp roasted chana

Method:

1. Dry roast poha, oats, and makhana till crisp.
2. Lightly roast nuts and chana.
3. Cool and grind to powder.
4. Store in an airtight jar.

Homemade cerelac (dry powder form) typically lasts:
	•	At room temperature: 1–2 months in an airtight container, if kept in a cool, dry place.
	•	In the refrigerator: up to 4 months.
	•	In the freezer: up to 6 months.

⚠️ Once cooked or mixed with water/milk, it should be used within 4–6 hours (room temp) or refrigerated for up to 24 hours.
